column1: # Korean rewrite rules (W) over kir nodes. They edit nodes and features, never text. Phases run disc then ko;
# inside a phase rules run in id order, each at most once per site. Cases: rules.cases.tsv (fix and keep); each
# case runs with its rule alone. Each rule is gated alone (spec/rewrite.md); --poc08 rule turns on only the rules
# listed in bridge/data/reader.tsv (`rewrite` rows). A rewrite may paraphrase only when meaning, nuance and register
# stay and no content or punctuation is added or dropped (STYLE-v3 §0); a note starting [off: …] says why a row is off.
#   pattern    node matchers [Kind lemma|lemma {feat=v|w,feat!=v}]:name, `?` optional, `...` gap inside the
#              clause, `^` clause start (line start or after 「 。 ！ ？), `$` clause end
#   condition  `-` or atoms joined by &: x.feat=v|w, x.feat!=v, x.clauselen<=n, x.prev.feat=v, x.next.feat=v;
#              a value @y.feat is node y's feature, - the empty value;
#              utt.level=v, utt.narration, utt.quote; `!` negates an atom
#   action     `;`-joined: set x.feat=v | copy x.feat=y.feat | del x | replace x [Kind lemma {feats}] |

column8: a change that happens to the subject needs no 버리다 (정해져 버렸다 → 정해졌다, 더러워져 버렸지만 → 더러워졌지만); an action keeps it (가 버렸다, 태워 버릴 거야)
[off: a comma after the source 、 is kept] K1: no comma after a line-initial conjunction or sentence adverb (refs: 하지만 9%, 그리고 2%, 그럼 12% with a comma); interjections keep it (네 90%, 아 100%)
[off: a comma after the source 、 is kept] K1: no comma after a connective clause (refs 8-10% with a comma, 0.7.5 28-46%)

[off: a comma after the source 、 is kept] no comma after a cause or tight-sequence -어서 clause (가서 산다, 몰라서 물었다); a conjunction that opens the next clause keeps it (하고 싶어서, 하지만); contrast and condition connectives keep theirs (comma.conn-1 lost 56.7%: -지만 10:44)
[off: fires on no dev line] a comma the source does not have
[off: a comma after the source 、 is kept] K1: no comma after a topic (refs 1%, 0.7.5 18%); a topic headed by a relative clause keeps it (끝낸 나는, 가지는 것은,), and so does a topic said twice (겨울은, 겨울은)
(으)로부터 → 에서, after a person 에게서 (한테서 in speech); G chooses by the noun's class. Not before 의 (씨로부터의 의뢰 → 에게서의 is worse)
(으)로부터 after a dictionary noun that is not a person (포켓, 결과, 정문) → 에서; not before another particle (씨로부터의, 취득으로부터가: a starting point)
(으)로부터 after a person (씨, 선생님, 그들) → 에게서, 한테서 in speech
(으)로부터 after a person noun the dictionaries carry without a person code (후보, 언니, 모두) → 에게서
의-chains: A의 B의 C → A B의 C when A is not a pronoun and no relative clause modifies A (마친 느낌의 학교의); a person noun A is fine (선생님 입술의)

column8: narration ends -는 것 같다 (ようだ, らしい) as -는 듯하다; -는 것 같은데, -다고 할까 keep 것 같다
casual speech says 너, not 당신 (6.2 vs 2.0 per 1,000 lines)
polite speech drops the addressee pronoun
casual speech to several people says 너희, not 당신들 (貴女達 → 너희)
same, when the reader keeps 들 apart
K5: state verbs do not take -고 있다 in the present (알고 있어 → 알아)
K5: verbs of feeling and remembering (class state) do not take -고 있다 in the present (기억하고 있어 → 기억해); 알다 and 생각하다 keep it (わかってる → 알아, 考えてる → 생각해 lost)
